slot.title: Matched grip and the full stroke
slot.lessonGoal: Hold the sticks in matched grip and play a relaxed full stroke that rebounds to its starting height.
objectives: Hold a drumstick in matched grip, with the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger
Describe a full stroke: the stick starts high, strikes the head, and rebounds to its starting height
Explain why letting the stick rebound keeps the hands relaxed

visuals.intent: A hand holding a drumstick in matched grip, seen so the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger is plain, for the Learner to copy.
The four moments of a full stroke in order, raised, striking, rebounding, and back at the starting height, so the Learner sees the stick come back up on its own.

lesson.title: Matched grip and the full stroke
lesson.lessonGoal: Hold the sticks in matched grip and play a relaxed full stroke that rebounds to its starting height.
objectives: Hold a drumstick in matched grip, with the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger
Describe a full stroke: the stick starts high, strikes the head, and rebounds to its starting height
Explain that letting the stick rebound naturally back up goes along with keeping the hands relaxed

sections.heading: A loose hold around a pivot

blocks.text: For your goal of playing the song, this lesson focuses on a relaxed hold and a stick that bounces back up.

The fulcrum is the pivot point where your thumb and index finger hold the stick [1]. In matched grip, your thumb lies along the stick, opposite the first knuckle of your index finger at the fulcrum [2]. Your other fingers wrap loosely around the stick rather than squeezing it [2].

sections.heading: Down and back to the starting height

blocks.text: A full stroke is a hit that starts high and bounces back to the same height [2][3]. Your wrist raises the stick tip eight inches above the drum [2]. The stick goes down to strike the drum, then bounces back up naturally [3].

Your thumb and index finger stay in contact with the stick while your wrist and fingers stay relaxed [3]. The stick follows a smooth path down and up, without stopping along the way [3]. A relaxed full stroke lets the stick bounce back to its starting height while your hand keeps a loose hold [2][3].

blocks.alt: Four panels show a stick raised above a drum, striking its surface, bouncing upward, and ending at its original height. Arrows show the downward and upward movement.
